title: 2026-11-05_Linux_XorDDoS_Botnet_Investigation_0b1
description: Investigate compromised Linux hosts and identify the malicious activity of the Linux/XorDDoS botnet.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity originating from several Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests these hosts may be compromised by the Linux/XorDDoS botnet malware. Your task is to investigate these hosts, identify the malicious activity, and implement appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the following hosts with the username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano':
- bot1 (192.168.70.10)
- bot2 (192.168.70.11)
- c2-server (192.168.70.5)

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on bot1. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.
2. List all services on the system using: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or those that don't match standard system services.
4. The suspicious service is named 'bot-beacon.service'. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use this command to list all services: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to beaconing activity.

levels.title: Determine Communication Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system on bot1. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Examine the suspicious service found in the previous task using: `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service`
2. Look for the ExecStart parameter which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
3. Inspect the script at `/usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh` to find the communication port with C2 server.
4. The C2 port number is 2222. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use this command to examine the service: `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service`

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart parameter in the service file.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The communication port is specified in the beacon script.

levels.title: Identify Scheduling Component
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically on bot1. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers on the system using: `systemctl list-timers --all`
2. Look for timers associated with the suspicious service found in previous tasks.
3. The timer responsible for scheduling the beacon service is named 'bot-beacon.timer'. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use this command to list all timers: `systemctl list-timers --all`

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers associated with the beacon service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer name follows the pattern of the service name with '.timer' appended.
